correlation-coefficient.def: A number, r, from -1 to +1 that describes the direction (its sign) and strength (its size) of the relationship between two variables.

positive-correlation.def: A relationship in which two variables tend to rise and fall together; r is above 0.

negative-correlation.def: A relationship in which one variable tends to fall as the other rises; r is below 0.

scatterplot.def: A graph of paired data in which each point is one person or case, placed by its values on two variables.

trend-line.def: The straight line that best fits the points on a scatterplot, showing the trend and allowing predictions. Also called a trend line.

directionality.def: In a correlation, not knowing which variable affects the other: A may lead to B, or B to A. Also called reverse causation.

illusory-correlation.def: A relationship that people believe exists between two things when the data show none, often because memorable cases stand out.
